output.title: nimbus nf-300 configuration and troubleshooting guide

sections.heading: ipsec and ikev2 tunnel setup
key_facts: For policy-based IKEv2 tunnels, avoid local selectors narrower than /30; use route-based VPN for host-to-host designs and enforce restrictions with firewall policy instead.
On 5.1.3 and 5.1.5, pin a single DH group on both peers, preferably group 14, and avoid mixed transform sets to prevent phase 2 resets.
On 5.0.8 and 5.0.9, keep the PFS group unchanged on both peers; if a change is required, apply the same group on both sides and clear the SA after the change.
If the platform is rekeying active traffic and a child SA change is required on 5.0.8 or 5.0.9, disable child SA rekey and schedule a manual tunnel restart during a maintenance window.

sections.heading: ha pair stability and resynchronization
key_facts: Place HA heartbeat links on a dedicated L2 segment that is independent of monitored interfaces to prevent oscillation.
If dedicated cabling is not immediately possible, set the HA monitor interval to 10 seconds so transient link events are less likely to trigger repeated failover.
On 5.0.9 after split-brain recovery, perform a full HA resync instead of relying on incremental replay.
After node return, keep failover links stable for at least 120 seconds so the replay queue can drain before you validate session state.

sections.heading: session-table tuning for asymmetric traffic
key_facts: On 5.2.0, if asymmetric routing is enabled for large-prefix traffic, disable it for the affected policy set when shard imbalance appears.
For concentrated /24 traffic, split the prefix into smaller policy groups so sessions distribute more evenly across shards.
Keep the busiest shard below 75 percent occupancy until a software fix is available, and verify distribution after each policy change.
Use session-table summary output to confirm that the hottest shard is not trending upward across successive samples.

sections.heading: ssl inspection cache and policy change handling
key_facts: On 5.2.0 and 5.2.2, increase the SSL inspection certificate cache size to 4096 entries to reduce eviction-driven bypass events.
If outbound TLS inspection starts bypassing intermittently after cache eviction, restart SSL inspection to clear stale pointers as a temporary recovery step.
Disable outbound inspection for the affected server group only if the cache increase does not keep evictions below 1,000 entries per hour.
Avoid changing SSL inspection policy while a threat database update is active, because activation can stall packet processing on 5.1.5.

sections.heading: firmware upgrade preparation and image staging
key_facts: Before upgrading from 5.0.x to 5.1.3 or 5.1.5, keep each checkpoint file under 4,000 entries and verify the running configuration immediately after reboot.
If the configuration contains more than 4,096 replay entries, split the upgrade into smaller chunks or export and re-import policy objects after first boot.
On 5.0.8, stage 5.0.9 images with SCP or USB rather than HTTPS so the boot loader does not reject a valid image because of padding.
Always verify the staged image hash before scheduling the reboot and confirm the image appears in software inventory.

sections.heading: threat database updates and timing control
key_facts: On 5.1.5, schedule threat database updates during a maintenance window and keep the signature bundle below 128 MB to avoid packet-processing stalls.
Set the update window to 02:00 through 02:15 when operationally feasible, and avoid SSL inspection policy changes until activation completes.
Use the threat database status output to confirm whether an update is active before making any inspection or policy changes.
If a large bundle is unavoidable, defer nonessential traffic-policy edits until the update has fully applied and the dataplane has returned to steady state.
